meta.source: WHO, IHR (2005) States Parties Self-Assessment Annual Reporting Tool (SPAR), 2nd edition, 2021: 15 capacities, 35 indicators, each scored at 5 levels.
meta.note: Level texts are short paraphrases (not WHO's wording) of levels 1, 3 and 5, written from the 2021 edition of the SPAR tool; each indicator has five levels. Levels build on each other: all attributes of a level must be in place before the next level counts. In the tool, countries can also tick "strength/best practice" next to their comments, so a country's own SPAR report may point to good practices. The links to JEE indicators and IHR benchmarks are a topic crosswalk made for this tool, not an official WHO mapping.

caps.name: Policy, legal and normative instruments to implement IHR
IHR coordination, National IHR Focal Point functions and advocacy
Points of entry (PoEs) and border health

indicators.title: Policy, legal and normative instruments
indicators.l1: No legal mapping of relevant instruments has been done.
indicators.l3: Gaps in the health sector are reviewed and the needed legal instruments and policies are developed or revised.
indicators.l5: Gaps are reviewed across all sectors and levels of government, and instruments are regularly evaluated and improved.
indicators.step: Level 2 has a legal analysis; level 3 adds identifying health-sector gaps and acting on them.

indicators.title: Gender equality in health emergencies
indicators.l1: No systematic assessment of gender gaps has been done in any IHR capacity.
indicators.l3: An action plan covers high-priority gender gaps in at least one capacity and sits in the annual workplan.
indicators.l5: Gender analysis is funded and action plans cover at least three capacities, with monitoring.
indicators.step: Level 2 has a gender assessment in at least one capacity; level 3 adds an action plan in the annual workplans.

indicators.title: National IHR Focal Point functions
indicators.l1: The focal point lacks terms of reference, authority, resources or round-the-clock access.
indicators.l3: The focal point has a clear mandate, resources and 24/7 access to WHO, but coordination with other sectors is still weak.
indicators.l5: The focal point is well positioned, trained and equipped, and its set-up is regularly reviewed.
indicators.step: Level 2 has a duty officer system but weak instruments; level 3 has a clear mandate and resources.

indicators.title: Multisectoral coordination mechanisms
indicators.l1: Mechanisms are missing or under development; coordination is ad hoc.
indicators.l3: Mechanisms are in place, shared and used nationally.
indicators.l5: Mechanisms work at all levels and are regularly exercised, reviewed and updated.
indicators.step: Level 2 has mechanisms that are not yet disseminated; level 3 disseminates and implements them nationally.

indicators.title: Advocacy for IHR implementation
indicators.l1: Advocacy mechanisms are missing and activities are ad hoc.
indicators.l3: Advocacy mechanisms are in place, shared and used nationally.
indicators.l5: Mechanisms work at all levels in a whole-of-society approach and are updated from lessons learned.
indicators.step: Level 2 has mechanisms that are not yet disseminated; level 3 disseminates and implements them nationally.

indicators.title: Financing for IHR implementation
indicators.l1: There is no financial planning or budget line; funding is extrabudgetary.
indicators.l3: Planning is based on identified gaps and needs, with budget or external funding and some monitoring.
indicators.l5: Budget is sufficient, predictable and flexible at all levels and monitored against objectives; the country can support others.
indicators.step: Level 2 has limited planning and funding for some sectors; level 3 bases planning on gaps and needs.

indicators.title: Financing for public health emergency response
indicators.l1: Emergency financing is not identified; funds are allocated ad hoc.
indicators.l3: Funds for immediate mobilisation are identified in advance for all relevant sectors.
indicators.l5: Emergency funds are available at all levels for timely use across sectors; the country can aid others.
indicators.step: Level 2 has structured reception and rapid use of funds; level 3 identifies funds in advance.

indicators.title: Specimen referral and transport system
indicators.l1: No system exists and transport is ad hoc, without SOPs.
indicators.l3: Referral and transport are organised for most priority diseases from subnational to national level.
indicators.l5: A sustainable, regularly reviewed system covers all specimen types at all levels.
indicators.step: Level 2 covers some priority diseases; level 3 covers most, from subnational to national.

indicators.title: Implementation of a laboratory biosafety and biosecurity regime
indicators.l1: National guidelines or regulations are under development.
indicators.l3: Guidelines or regulations are in place and used by all national laboratories.
indicators.l5: Regulations are regularly updated and exercised, with an oversight system.
indicators.step: Level 2 is implemented by some national laboratories; level 3 by all national laboratories.

indicators.title: Laboratory quality system
indicators.l1: National quality standards are missing or under development.
indicators.l3: Standards are developed and implemented nationally, including licensing of laboratories.
indicators.l5: All laboratories are licensed to international standards at all levels, with regular review.
indicators.step: Level 2 has standards but no implementation; level 3 adds implementation and licensing.

indicators.title: Laboratory testing capacity modalities
indicators.l1: The system supports only one or two modalities, such as rapid tests or microscopy.
indicators.l3: Nucleic acid testing and culture with sensitivity testing under quality assurance, plus access to sequencing.
indicators.l5: Full capacity including whole genome sequencing, in integrated networks with maximum coverage.
indicators.step: Level 2 adds serological tests with quality assurance; level 3 adds nucleic acid testing, culture and sequencing access.

indicators.title: Effective national diagnostic network
indicators.l1: Tier-specific diagnostic testing strategies are missing or under development.
indicators.l3: Tier-specific testing strategies exist but are not yet fully implemented.
indicators.l5: Strategies are implemented at national, intermediate and local levels and regularly exercised and updated.
indicators.step: Level 2 has developed strategies; level 3 has them in place but not yet fully implemented.

indicators.title: Early warning surveillance function
indicators.l1: National surveillance guidelines or SOPs are missing or under development.
indicators.l3: Guidelines are implemented nationally and give immediate and weekly reporting of events or data.
indicators.l5: Guidelines are implemented at all levels and the system is regularly exercised, reviewed and improved.
indicators.step: Level 2 has guidelines but no systematic immediate or weekly reporting; level 3 implements them.

indicators.title: Event management
indicators.l1: No process for managing detected events exists or it is under development.
indicators.l3: The process for managing detected events is implemented nationally.
indicators.l5: The process is implemented at all levels and regularly exercised, reviewed and updated.
indicators.step: Level 2 has a process that is not implemented; level 3 implements it nationally.

indicators.title: Human resources for implementation of IHR
indicators.l1: Staff in relevant sectors to detect, assess, report and respond to events are lacking.
indicators.l3: Qualified staff are available in all relevant sectors at national and intermediate levels.
indicators.l5: Staffing policies are documented, sustained and reviewed, and shared to help other countries.
indicators.step: Level 2 covers only the national level; level 3 extends to intermediate levels.

indicators.title: Workforce surge during a public health event
indicators.l1: No national multisectoral surge plan exists, or it is still being drafted.
indicators.l3: The surge plan is implemented nationally, with limited ability to move staff around the country.
indicators.l5: The plan works at all levels, with strong staff-sharing capacity, and is reviewed yearly.
indicators.step: Level 2 has a written plan; level 3 puts it into practice.

indicators.title: Planning for health emergencies
indicators.l1: No all-hazard, risk-informed emergency plan exists or it is in development.
indicators.l3: The plan is developed and being implemented nationally.
indicators.l5: The plan is implemented at all levels and improved through simulations and real events.
indicators.step: Level 2 has a plan that is not yet implemented; level 3 implements it nationally.

indicators.title: Management of health emergency response
indicators.l1: No incident management system linked to an emergency operations centre exists, or it is in development.
indicators.l3: The system is operational at the national level.
indicators.l5: The system supports all levels and is tested and improved through exercises and real events.
indicators.step: Level 2 has a developed but non-operational system; level 3 makes it operational nationally.

indicators.title: Emergency logistic and supply chain management
indicators.l1: The system is under development or cannot adequately support health emergencies.
indicators.l3: The system is developed and can adequately support emergencies nationally.
indicators.l5: The system operates at all levels and is regularly exercised and updated.
indicators.step: Level 2 is developed but still inadequate; level 3 is adequate at national level.

indicators.title: Case management
indicators.l1: National clinical guidelines for priority health events are missing or in development.
indicators.l3: Guidelines are developed and implemented nationally.
indicators.l5: Guidelines are implemented at all levels and regularly reviewed and updated.
indicators.step: Level 2 has guidelines that are not implemented; level 3 implements them nationally.

indicators.title: Utilization of health services
indicators.l1: Outpatient use is very low (under 1 visit per person per year).
indicators.l3: Outpatient use is satisfactory (2.0 or more visits per person per year) in urban and rural areas.
indicators.l5: Use is strong (3.0 or more visits) and utilisation and patient-experience data are reviewed yearly.
indicators.step: Level 2 is low use (1.0 to under 2.0 visits); level 3 is 2.0 or more.

indicators.title: Continuity of essential health services (EHS)
indicators.l1: No essential services package or emergency continuity plans exist.
indicators.l3: Essential services and continuity plans are defined, with national monitoring.
indicators.l5: Continuity mechanisms work at all levels and are tested and improved through simulations and real events.
indicators.step: Level 2 defines the services but has no continuity plans; level 3 adds plans and monitoring.

indicators.title: Infection prevention and control programmes
indicators.l1: No active national IPC programme or operational plan meeting WHO minimum requirements exists, or it is in development.
indicators.l3: A national IPC plan and guidelines exist, and selected facilities use multimodal strategies.
indicators.l5: IPC programmes work at national and facility level, with compliance reviewed, published and updated regularly.
indicators.step: Level 2 has a programme and guidelines that are not fully implemented; level 3 adds a national plan and facility implementation.

indicators.title: Health care-associated infections (HCAI) surveillance
indicators.l1: No national HCAI surveillance programme or strategic plan exists, or one is being drafted.
indicators.l3: A national plan runs through a national system, with selected secondary and tertiary facilities reporting and receiving feedback.
indicators.l5: Nationwide surveillance data are used continuously to guide prevention, and the quality of the system is regularly evaluated.

indicators.title: Safe environment in health facilities
indicators.l1: National standards for safe facility environments (WASH, IPC infrastructure, crowding, staffing) are missing or under development.
indicators.l3: The standards are applied in health facilities nationwide under a national plan.
indicators.l5: The standards are applied nationally and subnationally, regularly exercised, monitored and improved.

indicators.title: RCCE system for emergencies
indicators.l1: Coordination of risk communication and community engagement is ad hoc or in development.
indicators.l3: Coordination plans, SOPs and government arrangements are being implemented nationally.
indicators.l5: The mechanisms are built into emergency response at all levels and regularly reviewed.

indicators.title: Risk communication
indicators.l1: Public communication and media relations, including infodemic management, are ad hoc or in development.
indicators.l3: Communication mechanisms are developed and activities run nationally.
indicators.l5: Activities are coordinated across sectors at all levels, information is shared promptly and mechanisms are updated.

indicators.title: Community engagement
indicators.l1: Community engagement is ad hoc, or its guidelines are in development.
indicators.l3: Guidelines and SOPs are developed, shared and supported nationally.
indicators.l5: Engagement works at all levels, draws on socio-behavioural research and is regularly reviewed.

indicators.title: Core capacity requirements at all times for PoEs (airports, ports and ground crossings)
indicators.l1: A strategic risk assessment for individual points of entry, as part of the national risk assessment, is not yet complete.
indicators.l3: Some designated points of entry run core capacities that feed national biological or all-hazards surveillance.
indicators.l5: Core capacities at all designated points of entry are exercised, reviewed and improved regularly.

indicators.title: Public health response at points of entry
indicators.l1: Designated points of entry are developing public health emergency contingency plans.
indicators.l3: All designated points of entry have contingency plans for biological events, integrated into national response plans.
indicators.l5: All-hazard contingency plans at all designated points of entry are exercised, reviewed and updated regularly.

indicators.title: Risk-based approach to international travel-related measures
indicators.l1: A national multisectoral, risk-based process for adopting travel measures is missing or in development.
indicators.l3: The process is developed and implemented at national level.
indicators.l5: The process is implemented at all levels and updated after events or emergencies.

indicators.title: One Health collaborative efforts across sectors on activities to address zoonoses
indicators.l1: Human, animal and environment sectors work together on zoonoses only on an ad hoc basis.
indicators.l3: The sectors collaborate regularly at national level on one or more prioritised zoonoses, and have shown they can detect new or emerging ones at least occasionally.
indicators.l5: Joint prevention, detection and response capacities for endemic and emerging zoonoses are exercised, reviewed and improved regularly.
indicators.step: Level 2 has jointly mapped collaboration and agreed priority zoonoses; level 3 turns that into regular joint work at national level.

indicators.title: Multisectoral collaboration mechanism for food safety events
indicators.l1: A multisectoral mechanism with an INFOSAN Emergency Contact Point is being developed and used ad hoc.
indicators.l3: The mechanism and its communication channels exist at national, intermediate and local level where the country's structure calls for it.
indicators.l5: Mechanism and channels, nationally and internationally, are exercised, reviewed, evaluated and updated.
indicators.step: Level 2 has the mechanism and channels between the contact point, the IHR Focal Point and sectors nationally; level 3 extends them to lower levels.

indicators.title: Resources for detection and alert (chemical events)
indicators.l1: Surveillance mechanisms and resources for chemical events or poisoning are under development.
indicators.l3: A poisons information service or equivalent national service does surveillance for chemical exposures and alerts, on a 24/7 basis.
indicators.l5: An integrated public health surveillance system linked with environmental monitoring captures chemical exposure data from several sources (under development or in place).
indicators.step: Level 2 has ad hoc surveillance, for example a poison service that works office hours only; level 3 is a 24/7 national service.

indicators.title: Capacity and resources (radiation emergencies)
indicators.l1: Surveillance mechanisms and resources for radiation emergencies are under development.
indicators.l3: Access to specialised care for radiation injuries and to laboratory testing to assess radiation exposure is in place.
indicators.l5: Radiation emergency arrangements are formally exercised, reviewed and evaluated regularly, with improvements made.
indicators.step: Level 2 has inventoried radiation sources and mapped risks; level 3 adds care for radiation injuries and laboratory capacity. Level 4 adds expert advice and a stockpile.
